relations.rationale: A full room forming teams suggests the room is fuller, supporting Esme's pleasure at the full room.
Eagerness for rounds to start is consistent with teams whispering strategies, though not a direct cause.
Eagerness at the start doesn't directly determine reactions at the final tally.
Sami finishing ahead of Xavi is unrelated to laughter after wrong guesses.
Sami ahead of Xavi doesn't determine the relative finish of Xavi and Nell.
Sami ahead of Xavi is consistent with and slightly supports Sami being ahead of Nell if rankings are transitive with Xavi ahead of Nell, but alone doesn't guarantee it.
Sami's ranking relative to Xavi has no bearing on Esme's pleasure about room fullness.
Sami finishing ahead of Xavi is unrelated to the mixed reactions at final tally.
Engaging questions across topics could lead to wrong guesses and subsequent laughter, supporting the claim.
The content of questions is unrelated to the quality of Gus's voice.
Geography questions being part of the game supports the plausibility of Nell joking about her team's weak geography knowledge.
Laughter after wrong guesses is unrelated to Gus calling out scores.
Laughter after wrong guesses doesn't directly relate to Nell checking her team's tally.
Laughter after wrong guesses throughout the game supports the mixed cheers and groans at the final tally.
Xavi ahead of Nell is consistent with Sami being ahead of Nell if Sami is also ahead of Xavi, but doesn't itself establish it.
Xavi finishing ahead of Nell is unrelated to the general tension in the final round.
Xavi's ranking relative to Nell is unrelated to teams whispering strategies.
Xavi finishing ahead of Nell is unrelated to the night ending after tallying.
Gus calling out scores supports the claim that his voice was steady and clear, since it describes how he did so.
Gus announcing scores after each round would prompt Nell to check her team's tally, supporting the claim.
